A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Orient Anything and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original ShapeNet and ModelNet40 orientation experiments in Tables 1-2 and qualitative ShapeNet and Objaverse results in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains the original up-axis experiments and reports full-orientation Chamfer distances, adaptive prediction-set sizes, and qualitative results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the DGCNN quotient orienter, 24-class octahedral flipper, test-time augmentation, and conformal calibration described in Appendix B. The adaptive prediction-set output evaluated in v2 was already part of v1's method.

E1.justification: Both versions use all ShapeNet classes for training and orientation evaluation, ModelNet40 for up-axis generalization, and Objaverse for qualitative evaluation. The revised full-orientation experiments retain the same dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: V1's full-orientation Table 2 contains only the proposed pipeline. V2 adds Upright-Net-Random and Upright-Net-Oracle, constructing full orientations using random or ground-truth front axes. This introduces substantive comparisons into the previously comparator-free full-orientation evaluation; Table 1's upright comparator remains unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 replaces full-orientation accuracy at a 10-degree angular threshold with mean symmetric Chamfer distance, and replaces fixed top-4 evaluation with minimum distance over adaptive prediction sets. It specifies alpha=0.3 for this experiment. Appendix C also introduces a Chamfer success threshold estimated using 100 validation shapes rotated by 10 degrees. Training budgets and the upright evaluation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 revises the existing analysis of ambiguous orientations by comparing adaptive-set outputs with single predictions, adding a prediction-set-size histogram in Figure 8 and showing 20 complete sets in Figure 10. These replace fixed top-1/top-4 demonstrations and examine the number of choices presented to a user. Existing generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1's tables report point accuracies. V2 Table 2 introduces ± quantities alongside Chamfer means, but does not identify them as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, and conformal calibration was already described in v1.

E6.justification: Table 1's up-axis accuracies are unchanged. V1 Table 2's 68.3% top-1 and 85.8% top-4 accuracies are replaced by Chamfer means of 0.10801 for Upright-Net-Random, 0.05481 for Upright-Net-Oracle, 0.00856 for Orient Anything, and 0.00208 for Orient Anything-APS. V2 also reports median set size 2, with 90% containing at most 8 shapes. These are results under changed evaluation conditions, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The four propositions and their proofs are retained after relocation and renumbering. V1 Proposition 3.1 becomes v2 Proposition A.1. V2 Appendix A.3 relocates the existing bench non-uniqueness argument and explicitly writes the already-described Procrustes objective, without adding a substantive theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the same claims about the two-stage pipeline, state-of-the-art up-axis prediction, full-orientation estimation, and symmetry-based theoretical motivation. Class-independent orientation and human-assisted ambiguity resolution remain claimed contributions. The revised experiments change their supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly explains that canonical axes reflect human physical and functional judgments, motivates symmetry-insensitive evaluation, and discusses the tradeoff between adaptive-set accuracy and set size. It also interprets the new oracle/random comparisons. Existing qualifications about ambiguous front directions and poorer Objaverse flipper generalization remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new baselines' axis construction, specifies alpha=0.3 for adaptive-set evaluation, and provides the 100-shape recipe for qualitative success thresholds. Appendix B's architecture and training details remain unchanged. Calibration notation is ambiguous: the main text calls alpha the coverage probability, while Appendix B.3 uses 1-alpha as the confidence level.

R1.justification: V2 adds Zhou et al. (2022), Kaba et al. (2023), and Puny et al. (2022), connecting the work to task-conditioned alignment, learned canonicalization, and frame averaging. It also expands discussion of Poursaeed et al.'s classification approach. The principal positioning against upright-only methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands introductory explanations, promotes existing method paragraph headings into subsections, moves the impossibility proposition and bench example into Appendix A, and shortens the conclusion. It also adds an impact statement. These are localized editorial and structural revisions; the overall narrative order and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 converts the main text to two columns and substantially rearranges visual material. Figure 6 changes from logarithmic frequency histograms to empirical CDFs; Figure 8 becomes an adaptive-set-size histogram; Table 2 is restructured around four methods and Chamfer distances. Appendix galleries are redrawn, and Figure 10 displays complete adaptive sets.

improvement.justification: V2 better aligns full-orientation evaluation with shape symmetries and directly evaluates the previously described adaptive sets, including their sizes in Figures 8 and 10. These strengthen empirical support. However, the earlier angular-accuracy results are removed, and undefined ± quantities and inconsistent coverage notation limit the clarity and reproducibility of the new evidence.
